$comment: Design-System Alignment scores (roadmap 92.3). SOURCE OF TRUTH for what renders on component pages — never hand-type a score into a page. Each dimension is 0-3 with a checkable citation; `na` leaves the denominator. Full reasoning lives in .roundtable/scorecard-*.md; this file carries what the docs display. Re-take a score when a component's design changes, and update `scored` to that date.

definitions.$comment: What earns 3 on each dimension, and what a FAILURE looks like (roadmap 94.7). Written because three dimensions had scored 3 on 28 of 28 components — a value that never varies is not a measurement. Each definition names a component in this repo that scores below 3, so the dimension is known to be capable of failing.
definitions.hierarchy: 3 = no two affordances compete for primacy. `na` when the component presents fewer than two affordances — ranking one thing against nothing is vacuous, which is exactly why this read 3 on 28 of 28 before 94.7.
definitions.typography: 3 = no raw font-size; sizes come from the type scale or a density alias. Below 3 = a raw size off the scale. Fails today: amount (two 0.875em affixes), data-table (0.9em __col--code).
definitions.colour: 3 = zero raw colour outside @media print / forced-colors, and any state signal is two-channel. Below 3 = a raw colour on screen, or meaning carried by hue alone.
definitions.spacing: 3 = dimensions come from space tokens, or an intrinsic literal carries a comment saying why it is intrinsic. NOTE: this is a DEBT MARKER, not a quality signal — it is satisfiable by the scorer writing the comment, and once written it stays 3 forever. Read it as "has this file been through a scoring pass", not as "is this well spaced".
definitions.interaction: 3 = for a component shipping a behavior, the page states what the PLATFORM provides versus what the behavior adds, so a reader knows what they lose by not running the JS. `na` when the component ships no behavior. Below 3 = a behavior-backed component whose page never draws that line.
definitions.content: 3 = the page names at least one context where this component is the WRONG choice, and what to use instead. Below 3 = the page says only what the component is and how to use it. The six that failed when this definition was written (approval-workflow, file-upload, filters, offcanvas, ordered-list, tag-input) were fixed in 94.8; the dimension has demonstrated it can fail, and the citations quote the sentence that clears it.
definitions.fit: 3 = the docs place the component in the contexts the field matrix assigns it, including where it does NOT belong. 0 = prescribed in no context at all. Fails today: date (deprecated, zero screens use it).
